predecessors.name: K'iche' kingdom
predecessors.text: the Kaqchikel country around Iximche in Chimaltenango Department; the pages give no frontier

successors.name: Spanish Empire
successors.text: the Kaqchikel country around Iximche in Chimaltenango Department; the pages give no frontier

ledger.x: c. 1470: the Kaqchikel, 'forced to flee the K'iche' capital', found Iximche as their own capital.
1475: 'After the death of king K'iq'ab in 1475 the K'iche' were engaged in warfare' with the Kaqchikel and the Tz'utujil; the Kaqchikel 'soundly defeated their former overlords around 1491'.
1522: 'a peace accord was made' between the K'iche' and the Kaqchikel.
14 April 1524: the Spanish are 'invited into Iximche and... well received by the lords Belehe Qat and Cahi Imox'; the Kaqchikel pact with Alvarado follows and he demands 'tribute'.
28 August 1524: the Kaqchikel 'abandon their city and flee to the forests and hills'; the alliance is over.
Early September 1524: ten days after 28 August 'the Spanish declared war on the Kaqchikel'; the revolt lasts until 1530.
9 May 1530: 'exhausted by the warfare that had seen the deaths of their best warriors' the two Kaqchikel kings return from the wilds and surrender the next day at Ciudad Vieja.
May 1530: the Kaqchikel country passes under Spanish rule at the surrender.
9-10 May 1530: the Kaqchikel kingdom ends with the surrender of its two kings.

wars.name: K'iche'-Kaqchikel and Tz'utujil wars
wars.outcome: The Kaqchikel defeated the K'iche' around 1491 and crushed an internal Akajal and Tukuche revolt on 20 May 1493; 'in 1522 a peace accord was made'.

wars.name: Kaqchikel revolt against the Spanish
wars.outcome: After the alliance of April 1524 the Kaqchikel fled Iximche on 28 August 1524 and fought on; the Spanish abandoned Tecpan in 1527, burned the palace of the Ahpo Xahil (a group of sixteen Spanish deserters, 9 February 1526) and the Kaqchikel kings surrendered…

certainty.note: No frontier is described on any page opened.
